After the massive real estate expansion that swept through the South Bay in 2025, Apple is once again expanding its footprint in Sunnyvale. Here are the details.

Apple continues to expand its real estate portfolio

According to the Mercury News (republished by AppleInsider), Apple has agreed to lease a 125,800-square-foot office building located at 580 North Mary Avenue in Sunnyvale.

This deal marks Apple's first major real estate move publicly announced in the area in 2026. In 2025, Apple spent over $1 billion expanding its South Bay footprint in a flurry of activity.

The expansion included the $166.9 million purchase of the three-building Cupertino Gateway complex, the $350 million acquisition of the two-building Mathilda Commons campus in Sunnyvale, and the $365 million purchase of the adjacent four-building Mathilda Campus.

Apple subsequently spent an additional $216 million to acquire two buildings on Stevens Creek Boulevard in Cupertino, bringing its 2025 Bay Area expansion to a total of over 1.5 million square feet of office and lab space.

Speaking of Apple's new lease, the Mercury News noted that this deal comes as office leasing activity in the South Bay region picks up again, with vacancy rates improving compared to both the previous quarter and the same period last year:

According to Colliers, the office vacancy rate in the South Bay region for the second quarter of 2026 stood at 14.1%. Colliers defines the market area as Santa Clara County and Fremont.

In addition to Apple, the report also noted that Amazon has agreed to lease 316,600 square feet of office space located at 1000 Enterprise Way in Sunnyvale.
